title: Adapting a hospital group pain self-management programme to improve reach and completion: an implementation study
abstract: Objective: to evaluate the reach, completion and outcomes of three adaptations to a group pain self-management programme. Design: single-clinic implementation study guided by RE-AIM, with adaptations introduced in sequence during 2027 and follow-up of people who leave. Primary outcome: completion of six or more of eight sessions. Results and conclusions will be written after the 2027 groups.
introduction: Group pain self-management programmes lose many participants early. The clinic's completion is 41 percent and its waiting list seven months. A recorded search returned no records on the planned adaptations, so the clinic's own study is the main source of evidence.
methods: Barriers recorded at referral; orientation call and hybrid option from the first 2027 group and an evening group if approved; attendance at every session; brief outcome checks and conversations with people who leave; run chart of completion by group against the baseline median; StaRI reporting.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present reach, completion by group and adaptation, completion by barrier, pain interference for completers and leavers, group connection, fidelity and themes from conversations with leavers.
discussion: The discussion will interpret changes in completion against the run chart rules and the sequence of adaptations, and state which adaptations the clinic will keep.
limitations: Single clinic; overlapping adaptations; not powered for a confirmatory comparison; low response from leavers is likely.
conclusion: To be written after the 2027 groups; it will not claim that any adaptation causes higher completion.
summary: StaRI-structured draft with results left empty until data exist.
